items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: This was my first job when I got out of college was with Buddy Rich... I got to play with Buddy for two years

ctx.x: Yeah I mean you know certainly playing — I mean for a brass player it’s kind of interesting. This was my first job when I got out of college was with Buddy Rich, which I’m still to this day grateful for that opportunity. It was awesome. He, you know he was a lunatic in his own kind of way but a genius in another way. And I was so thrilled to get the call on that. I actually left Eastman three months before graduation, much to the chagrin of my mom and everybody else that, “You’re making a mistake.” I knew I…

player. But certainly in terms of improvisation if I play a note that’s — I’m not intending, and I can’t figure out my way to get out of it, then that’s kind of a wrong note. But that’s not to say that you can play unintended notes that don’t lead you down another path that really opens up something else that you weren’t even thinking of when that note occurred.
